rule: Declare list-valued service schema fields with a real voluptuous list validator such as vol.All(cv.ensure_list, [str]), never with a bare Python type annotation like list[str].
trigger: A vol.Schema in an integration's services.py using a typing construct (list[str], dict[str, str]) as the validator for a Required/Optional key.
rationale: list[str] is not a voluptuous validator: it silently coerces a single string into a list of its characters, producing confusing validation errors for YAML and service calls that pass one value.

evidence.excerpt: In voluptuous this is not a safe list validator

rule: Resolve a config entry from a service call with the core helper homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry instead of hand-rolling entry-exists / correct-domain / loaded-state checks in the integration.
trigger: An integration service handler defining its own _async_get_config_entry-style function that looks up hass.config_entries by id and raises ServiceValidationError for missing/unloaded entries.
rationale: The core helper already performs the same validation and emits the standardized error translations, so duplicating it diverges error messages from every other integration.

evidence.excerpt: Home Assistant provides a standard helper for this: homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry

rule: When an entity platform method maps a Home Assistant enum value onto a vendor constant, validate membership before indexing and raise HomeAssistantError, so an unsupported mode never escapes as a raw KeyError.
trigger: An async_set_* entity method indexing a module-level HA-to-vendor mapping dict (e.g. HVAC_TO_WF_MODE[hvac_mode]) inside a try block that only catches library or ValueError exceptions.
rationale: Service calls can carry any value of the HA enum, including ones the device does not support; an uncaught KeyError surfaces as an internal traceback rather than an actionable error.

evidence.excerpt: HVAC_TO_WF_MODE[hvac_mode] will raise KeyError for any unexpected/unsupported value

rule: Do not add strings.json entries or icons for preset modes that already exist as core common presets; use the core PRESET_* constants in code and let the built-in translations and icons apply.
trigger: New state_attributes.preset_mode entries in an integration's strings.json or icons.json naming standard presets such as eco, comfort, away, boost.
rationale: Common presets are already translated and iconed in core; re-declaring them in an integration duplicates translations and drifts from the shared vocabulary.

evidence.excerpt: Eco and comfort are already built in common preset modes, so you can omit

rule: Do not create entities for static device metadata; firmware version, mDNS name and similar constants belong in the device registry entry, not in the state machine.
trigger: A new sensor entity description whose value is a device identity or configuration constant (firmware version, mdns name, serial, IP) rather than a changing measurement, even under EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC.
rationale: Values that never change do not belong in the state machine and are already carried on the device registry entry; each one adds a permanently-recorded state for no benefit.

evidence.excerpt: mdns name is static, so doesn't belong in the state machine

rule: Key an entity's icons.json entry by the exact translation_key set on its entity description, not by the sensor's internal key.
trigger: An added icons.json entity key under a platform that does not literally match the translation_key of the corresponding EntityDescription.
rationale: Icon lookup is performed by translation_key, so a mismatched key silently fails and the entity renders with no icon.

evidence.excerpt: Use the translation_key (uv_index) as the icons.json entity key

rule: Bound any integration-held cache keyed by a client- or peer-supplied identifier with a global cap or TTL, not just a per-key size limit.
trigger: A dict on an integration object indexed by an externally supplied id (session id, request id) that is written on inbound messages and only pruned per entry.
rationale: A per-key cap still lets a caller allocate unbounded keys by inventing new ids, growing the dict without limit and exhausting memory.

evidence.excerpt: the number of distinct session_id keys in _pending_candidates is currently unbounded

rule: Reuse the integration's existing const.py constant when another platform module already defines the same tuning value; do not repeat the literal in a second platform.
trigger: A numeric literal in an integration platform module (delay, timeout, threshold) duplicating a value already named in that integration's const.py or another platform file.
rationale: The same wait-then-refresh behaviour is implemented in several platforms of one integration; keeping the value in const.py means it is tuned in one place instead of drifting per platform.

evidence.excerpt: Avoid hardcoding the refresh delay. switch.py already uses the SWITCH_REFRESH_DELAY constant from const.py

rule: Include the idle notification value 0 in not_states for Z-Wave notification binary sensors so the entity clears when the device reports idle.
trigger: A NotificationZWaveJSEntityDescription whose not_states set lists only the specific event enum members and omits 0.
rationale: Z-Wave notification state variables latch; without the idle value in not_states the binary sensor never turns back off.

evidence.excerpt: I think we need to include the idle state 0 here too.

rule: Adding a NewZWaveDiscoverySchema for a value that a legacy DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS entry already matches must preserve the existing entities: set allow_multi and adjust the legacy catch-all's not_states, or migrate the whole notification type and add it to MIGRATED_NOTIFICATION_TYPES.
trigger: A new NewZWaveDiscoverySchema entry in zwave_js covering a notification value or command class that legacy discovery schemas already produce entities for.
rationale: New-style schemas run before the legacy list and mark the value discovered, so the legacy schema is skipped and its entity silently disappears from users' installations; for latching notifications that also removes the only way to reset the state.

evidence.excerpt: New-style schemas are evaluated before the legacy DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS

rule: Gate a report_usage deprecation warning on the deprecated condition actually being present, so callers that do not use the deprecated pattern never see it logged.
trigger: A report_usage call with breaks_in_ha_version placed on a common code path in core helpers without a check that the deprecated feature is in use.
rationale: An unconditional report fires on every call of the surrounding helper, producing a false breaking-change warning and significant log noise for integrations doing nothing wrong.

evidence.excerpt: Only log/report this deprecation when the entry actually has update listeners

rule: Keep a guard that prevents a registry's _async_load from running more than once.
trigger: Removal of the loaded-event assertions or any other once-only guard from a registry _async_load in homeassistant/helpers.
rationale: _async_load calls async_setup_cleanup, so a second invocation registers the cleanup listeners again and duplicates cleanup work and events.

evidence.excerpt: Reintroduce a guard to prevent _async_load from running more than once

rule: Do not assume a sibling registry is set up when one registry helper calls another; guard dr.async_get / er.async_get so lookups still work with mocked or partially initialised registries.
trigger: A new dr.async_get(self._hass) or er.async_get(hass) call added inside an entity_registry or device_registry method that previously touched only its own data.
rationale: Tests and partially initialised setups call registry lookups before the other registry exists, so an unguarded cross-registry access breaks lookups that used to work.

evidence.excerpt: Guard dr.async_get() so entity lookups still work in tests/mocked registries

rule: Do not key a long-lived registry or cache by entity_id; entity_id changes at runtime on registry rename, so track the key used at insert time or keep it in sync on entity_id updates.
trigger: A module-level or hass-data dict indexed by entity.entity_id in async_added_to_hass and deleted by entity.entity_id in async_will_remove_from_hass.
rationale: After a registry rename the delete raises KeyError and leaves a stale key behind, breaking every later lookup through that dict.

evidence.excerpt: get_group_entities is keyed by entity.entity_id, but entity_id can change at runtime

rule: Match entity registry entries on domain and platform in addition to unique_id; unique_id alone is not unique across integrations.
trigger: An entity_registry_updated event handler or registry lookup whose condition tests only entry.unique_id against a set of known ids.
rationale: unique_id is only unique within a platform and domain, so an unrelated integration's entity with a colliding id triggers cache invalidation and state updates for the wrong entity.

evidence.excerpt: without verifying that the entry belongs to the same domain and platform

rule: Keep the dependency between core helper modules one-way: do not add a top-level import that closes a cycle between helpers modules; use a function-local import or move the logic into the module that already owns the dependency.
trigger: A new top-level `from .<helper> import ...` in homeassistant/helpers/ where the imported module already imports the importing one.
rationale: helpers.network already imports helpers.http for current_request; the reverse top-level import creates a circular import that breaks as soon as either module touches the other at import time.

evidence.excerpt: introduces a circular import (helpers.network imports helpers.http for current_request)

rule: Use plain string values, not enum members, in selector option and mode lists so voluptuous validation errors show the user-facing string rather than an enum repr.
trigger: A selector constant in homeassistant/helpers/selector.py listing StrEnum members that are later fed to vol.In or exposed in a selector config.
rationale: vol.In error messages and comparisons render the enum representation, leaking internal class names into messages that users and the frontend see.

evidence.excerpt: Use plain string values so vol.In error messages don't expose enum representations
